rework_history: The first runtime-adapter candidate accepted a RootPermit-v1 that authenticated only action and target, so a complete reconciliation decision could be substituted.
RootPermit-v2 corrected that authority boundary by separating action-only issuance from reconciliation issuance and binding the latter to the complete typed EffectResolution.
The first corrected receipt falsely classified its root-issued task envelope as worker-owned; root committed the envelope and corrective lease before refreezing the worker set.
The next receipt named imprecise semantic ownership; the final WorkerResult enumerates the exact leased symbols and generated outputs.
closed_findings: Every reconcile mutation verifies a RootPermit-v2 bound to the exact complete EffectResolution before workspace mutation.
Resume and recover routes reject reconciliation permits, reconciliation rejects action-only permits, and RootPermit-v1 input is rejected.
Candidate, source, workspace, operation, target, expected head, expiry, nonce, actor, and exact effect decision remain bound across dispatch and replay checks.
Read-only planning and refusal paths preserve recursive zero-write behavior.
Race, replay, stale-head, mutation, substitution, downgrade, recovery, and fresh-process test journeys pass through the production-exported adapter source.

root_acceptance_limit: Production-exported source-local orchestration runtime adapter behavior with exact decision-bound permit verification, typed refusal, replay/race controls, and recursive zero-write read paths.

invalidation_rule: Any change to an accepted runtime-adapter artifact, RootPermit-v2 authority, effect-resolution binding, product module export, dependency named by the WorkerResult, or named contract test immediately reopens this acceptance.
no_claim_statement: This acceptance does not claim a production issuer, durable replay ledger, public command behavior, installed runtime, representative supported-host journeys, readiness, release, node closure, or goal completion.
